title: Operator gates and screens: preview, release, design, control room
description:
Split out of epic-8ebe64173d934f72a339c32bc2eaaf7d ("Create product production") on 2026-09-05 by architect-b63fabf3, with the human's authorisation, when that epic measured 101 non-archived rows against the 40 advisory ceiling. This epic holds the browser-facing DECISION SURFACES: the operator sees something the fleet produced, and says yes or no to it.

Four capability bands, kept in ONE epic on purpose (see architectureNotes): Working preview / Gate 2 (order 30-33), Release / Gate 3 (order 40-43), Control-room completeness (order 50-53), and the Design step (order 60-63).
architectureNotes:
WHY THESE FOUR BANDS ARE ONE EPIC AND NOT FOUR.

`preview.decide`, `release.decide` and `design.submit` each publish a command kind through the SAME shared roster: packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts, its hand-transcribed runtime-contract.test.ts, the regenerated control-room client, and the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors (two of which live under apps/control-room and are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg). On the daemon side they contend on daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-families.ts, daemon-command-registry.ts and three hand-written test rosters carrying count literals.

That contention is why task-20b7d6bb, task-54b74b80, task-bda0eeac and task-06ac0da1 all declare dependsOn against the preview rows: it is FILE-COLLISION SEQUENCING, not a capability dependency. Splitting these bands into separate epics would leave each worker unable to read the neighbouring row's completionSummary through get_context.epicSiblings, and the rails direct exactly that read INSTEAD of re-measuring HEAD. The digest-mirror census going stale (task-40e52fa8, blocked once on it) is what that failure looks like.

THE ROSTER PATTERN, measured twice on this board: publishing one new command kind end to end is a FOUR-ROW job, not one - shared contract + digest mirrors (6 files), the refusal vocabulary module, daemon wiring and operator fence, then the behaviour. The shared-contract slice alone is six files and has zero headroom against the 10-file plan cap.

EPIC-FINAL: this epic has no single integration-and-hardening row. Its band parents (task-f3edb8fb Gate 2, task-2a345b2e Gate 3, task-e7a20a49 control room, task-8a6d6660 design) are integration-shaped for their own bands, and the whole-product proof stays on task-161b7e9d in the parent epic, which declares dependsOn against all of them. Decide deliberately whether to add one here rather than letting it default.
epicRails: A COMMAND KIND IS A FOUR-ROW JOB. Shared contract + all four digest mirrors; the refusal vocabulary with its closed code->layer map; daemon wiring and operator fence; then the behaviour. Do not plan it as one row - the shared-contract slice alone is six files against a 10-file cap, and the daemon roster is another six.

ANY ROW THAT ADDS A RUNTIME COMMAND KIND MUST RUN `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` AND CENSUS THE DIGEST MIRRORS with a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types. apps/control-room is in none of `pnpm test` (the root vitest include has no apps/**), `pnpm typecheck`, or `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` - so a forgotten mirror ships two hard-throwing tests behind three green gates.

NEVER FREEZE A ROSTER COUNT IN A DoD. Every count literal in this epic's shared files is one a concurrent kind-publishing row moves first. Write the gate as "run the leg, take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative", and declare dependsOn on the sibling kind's rows so two rows never bump the same literal at once.
HUMAN GATES ARE HUMAN-ONLY: operator-only principal, MCP-excluded, and every refusal carrying a stable code asserted WITH its layer - never merely that the operation failed.
